1.headline: Bulgaria has its first woman president
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Bulgaria has a new president. Her name is Iliana Iotova. She is the first woman to win this job in a vote. On Sunday, people voted for the second time. She got about 58 percent of the votes.
Bulgaria is a country in Europe. Before, Iotova was the vice president. In January, the old president left his job. Now he is the prime minister. So Iotova did the president's job for a while.
In Bulgaria, the president does not have much power. The prime minister leads the country. But this is a first for Bulgaria.
Again, Iliana Iotova is the new president of Bulgaria. She is the first woman to win the job.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
불가리아에 새 대통령이 생겼습니다. 이름은 일리아나 요토바입니다. 그녀는 투표로 이 자리에 오른 첫 여성입니다. 일요일에 사람들이 두 번째로 투표했습니다. 그녀는 약 58퍼센트의 표를 얻었습니다.
불가리아는 유럽에 있는 나라입니다. 전에 요토바는 부통령이었습니다. 1월에 이전 대통령이 자리에서 물러났습니다. 지금 그는 총리입니다. 그래서 요토바가 한동안 대통령의 일을 했습니다.

다시 말씀드리면, 일리아나 요토바가 불가리아의 새 대통령입니다. 그녀는 이 자리에 오른 첫 여성입니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

2.headline: Bulgaria elects its first woman president
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Bulgaria has elected its first woman president. Her name is Iliana Iotova. On Sunday, voters chose between the top two candidates. This second vote is called a runoff. According to news reports, Iotova won about 57.6 percent of the vote. Her rival, Andrey Gyurov, won about 39.5 percent.

Iotova already knows the job well. She was the vice president. In January, President Rumen Radev quit his job. He wanted to run in a different election for parliament. He won, and now he is the prime minister. Since January, Iotova has done the president's job. Radev's party supported her.

In Bulgaria, the president has limited power. The prime minister leads the government. Radev and Iotova both want the war in Ukraine to end through talks. Radev has also spoken against sanctions on Russia. Sanctions are punishments, like limits on trade. Bulgaria is a member of the European Union.
To sum up, Iliana Iotova won Bulgaria's presidential election. She is the first woman elected to the job.
Thank you for listening.

3.headline: Bulgaria elects its first woman president in a runoff
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Bulgaria has elected its first woman president. According to news reports, Iliana Iotova won a runoff election on Sunday. A runoff is a second round of voting between the top two candidates. Iotova received about 57.6 percent of the vote. Her rival, Andrey Gyurov, got about 39.5 percent. Almost 3 percent of voters chose the option "I support no one."

Iotova is not new to the job. She was the country's vice president under Rumen Radev. In January, Radev resigned as president to run in the parliamentary election. He won that race and is now the prime minister. Since then, Iotova has served as acting president. Acting means she did the job for a time without being elected to it. Radev's party, Progressive Bulgaria, supported her campaign. In the first round on October 25, she came first with about 34.6 percent.

Why does this matter? In Bulgaria, the president has limited powers. The prime minister usually leads the government. Still, the result makes Radev's political group stronger. Radev has opposed sanctions on Russia. Sanctions are penalties, like trade limits, that countries use to put pressure on another country. Both Radev and Iotova have called for a diplomatic end to the war in Ukraine. Some analysts describe their camp as friendly toward Moscow. Bulgaria is a member of the European Union and NATO, so its partners will watch closely.
To sum up, Iliana Iotova won Bulgaria's presidential runoff with about 57.6 percent of the vote. She is the first woman ever elected to the job.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
불가리아가 첫 여성 대통령을 뽑았습니다. 보도에 따르면 일리아나 요토바가 일요일 결선 투표에서 이겼습니다. 결선 투표란 상위 두 후보를 두고 하는 두 번째 투표를 말합니다. 요토바는 약 57.6퍼센트를 얻었습니다. 경쟁자 안드레이 규로프는 약 39.5퍼센트를 얻었습니다. 유권자의 3퍼센트 가까이는 '아무도 지지하지 않음'을 골랐습니다.

요토바에게 이 일은 처음이 아닙니다. 그녀는 루멘 라데프 대통령 아래에서 부통령이었습니다. 1월에 라데프는 총선에 나가기 위해 대통령직을 사임했습니다. 그는 그 선거에서 이겨 지금은 총리입니다. 그 뒤로 요토바가 대통령 권한대행을 맡아 왔습니다. 권한대행이란 선출되지 않은 채 한동안 그 일을 맡는 것을 뜻합니다. 라데프의 정당 '진보 불가리아'가 그녀의 선거 운동을 지지했습니다. 10월 25일 1차 투표에서 그녀는 약 34.6퍼센트로 1위를 했습니다.

4.headline: Iotova becomes Bulgaria's first elected female president
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Bulgaria has elected a woman as president for the first time in its history. According to near-final results, Iliana Iotova won Sunday's runoff with roughly 57.6 percent of the vote, comfortably ahead of challenger Andrey Gyurov, who took about 39.5 percent. Just under 3 percent of ballots were cast for the option "I support no one," and turnout was reported to be low.

Iotova is hardly a newcomer. She served as vice president under Rumen Radev, who stepped down as head of state in January to contest the parliamentary election. Radev went on to win that vote and now serves as prime minister, while Iotova has been acting president since his resignation. Radev's party, Progressive Bulgaria, backed her campaign. In the first round on October 25, she finished ahead with around 34.6 percent, while Gyurov came second with about 32 percent. The two had been separated by only a few points at that stage.

The presidency in Bulgaria carries limited powers. Its decisions can be overruled by a simple majority in parliament, and the office is generally seen as secondary to that of the prime minister. Still, the president represents Bulgaria abroad and remains a visible figure in public life. Even so, the result strengthens Radev's political camp. Radev has opposed sanctions on Russia, and analysts quoted in news reports describe the camp as friendly toward Moscow. Both he and Iotova have called for a diplomatic end to the war in Ukraine. Because Bulgaria belongs to both the European Union and NATO, its partners are likely to follow the new president's positions closely.
To sum up, Iliana Iotova has become Bulgaria's first elected female president, winning the runoff with about 57.6 percent in a result that further strengthens Prime Minister Rumen Radev's camp.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.

요토바는 결코 신인이 아닙니다. 그녀는 루멘 라데프 아래에서 부통령을 지냈는데, 라데프는 총선에 출마하려고 1월에 국가원수 자리에서 물러났습니다. 라데프는 그 선거에서 이겨 지금 총리를 맡고 있고, 요토바는 그의 사임 이후 대통령 권한대행을 맡아 왔습니다. 라데프의 정당 '진보 불가리아'가 그녀의 선거 운동을 지원했습니다. 10월 25일 1차 투표에서 그녀는 약 34.6퍼센트로 앞섰고, 규로프는 약 32퍼센트로 2위였습니다. 그 단계에서 두 사람의 차이는 몇 퍼센트포인트에 불과했습니다.

5.headline: Bulgaria hands presidency to a woman for the first time
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Bulgaria has, for the first time, entrusted its presidency to a woman chosen at the ballot box. Iliana Iotova, who had been serving as acting head of state, comfortably carried Sunday's runoff, securing roughly 57.6 percent of the vote, according to near-final results. Her challenger, Andrey Gyurov, trailed with about 39.5 percent, while close to 3 percent of voters opted for the ballot's "I support no one" choice. Turnout was reported to be low, a familiar pattern in a country that has held repeated elections in recent years.

Iotova's victory caps a remarkable reshuffle at the top of Bulgarian politics. She spent years as vice president alongside Rumen Radev, who resigned the presidency in January in order to throw his hat into the ring for parliament. That gamble paid off: Radev's Progressive Bulgaria party won the legislative contest, propelling him into the prime minister's office and leaving Iotova to hold the fort as acting president. With Radev's party firmly behind her, she topped the first round on October 25 with around 34.6 percent, edging out Gyurov, who finished on roughly 32 percent, before pulling decisively ahead in the second.

Under Bulgaria's system, the presidency wields only limited levers of power; its decisions can be overruled by a simple parliamentary majority, and it is widely regarded as playing second fiddle to the prime minister. Even so, the head of state represents the country abroad and offers a prominent platform in national debate. More significantly, the outcome consolidates Radev's grip on both the government and the presidency. Radev has long opposed sanctions on Russia, and analysts cited in news reports characterize his camp as Kremlin-friendly. Both he and Iotova have advocated a negotiated settlement to the war in Ukraine. For a member of both the European Union and NATO, that stance is likely to draw close scrutiny from allies in Brussels and beyond.

To sum up, Iliana Iotova has made history as Bulgaria's first elected female president, winning the runoff with nearly 58 percent of the vote and cementing the dominance of Prime Minister Rumen Radev's political camp.
Thank you for listening.

1.headline: Hackers attack supermarket fridges in Europe
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Some supermarkets in Europe had a big problem. Hackers attacked their fridges and freezers. Hackers are people who break into computers. This is called a cyberattack. It happened in five countries, like Sweden and Belgium.
In some stores, the freezers got very hot. One freezer went up to 50 degrees. The food went bad. The stores had to throw it away. One company fixed its problem in a few minutes.
Last month, the same thing happened in France. No one has said who did it.
Again, hackers attacked supermarket fridges in Europe. Some food went bad.
Thank you for listening.

들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

2.headline: Cyberattacks hit supermarket fridges in five countries
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Supermarkets in five European countries had trouble with their fridges and freezers. Fridges keep food cold, and freezers keep food frozen. According to news reports, hackers attacked the computer systems that control them. This kind of attack is called a cyberattack. The countries were Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia.

In some stores, hackers made the freezers very hot, up to 50 degrees Celsius. The food inside went bad, so stores had to throw it away. In Belgium, one big chain said several dozen stores had problems. In Sweden, another chain said six stores were affected. One company in Estonia said it fixed its problem in a few minutes.

A similar attack happened in France last month. It hit hundreds of stores. In France, the hackers seemed to target old systems. No one has said who is behind the new attacks. This shows that machines connected to the internet can also be attacked.
To sum up, hackers attacked supermarket fridges in five countries in Europe. Some stores lost food.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
유럽 다섯 나라의 슈퍼마켓에서 냉장고와 냉동고에 문제가 생겼습니다. 냉장고는 음식을 차갑게, 냉동고는 음식을 얼린 채로 보관합니다. 보도에 따르면 해커들이 이를 제어하는 컴퓨터 시스템을 공격했습니다. 이런 공격을 사이버 공격이라고 합니다. 피해를 입은 나라는 스웨덴, 벨기에, 룩셈부르크, 아일랜드, 에스토니아입니다.
어떤 가게에서는 해커들이 냉동고를 섭씨 50도까지 뜨겁게 만들었습니다. 안에 있던 음식이 상해서 가게들은 그것을 버려야 했습니다. 벨기에에서는 한 대형 체인이 수십 개 매장에 문제가 생겼다고 밝혔습니다. 스웨덴에서는 다른 체인이 매장 6곳이 피해를 입었다고 밝혔습니다. 에스토니아의 한 회사는 몇 분 만에 문제를 고쳤다고 말했습니다.
지난달 프랑스에서도 비슷한 공격이 있었습니다. 수백 개 매장이 피해를 입었습니다. 프랑스에서 해커들은 오래된 시스템을 노린 것으로 보였습니다. 이번 공격의 배후가 누구인지는 아무도 밝히지 않았습니다. 이 일은 인터넷에 연결된 기계도 공격받을 수 있다는 것을 보여 줍니다.
정리하면, 해커들이 유럽 다섯 나라의 슈퍼마켓 냉장고를 공격했습니다. 일부 가게는 음식을 잃었습니다.

3.headline: Hackers target supermarket freezers in Europe
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Supermarkets in several European countries say their fridges and freezers were attacked by hackers. According to the Associated Press, the problems hit stores in Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia. In some stores, the temperature inside the units was raised to 50 degrees Celsius. That is hot enough to spoil food very quickly. Some shops had to throw away food that went bad.

In Sweden, the ICA group said a limited number of its stores were affected. Another chain, Coop, reported problems at six stores. In Belgium, the chain Delhaize called it an "IT incident." It affected several dozen stores, mostly in Belgium and a few in Luxembourg. Carrefour Belgium said 15 of its more than 700 stores were hit. In Estonia, the head of a company that makes the cooling technology said attackers got into a computer that controls the fridges. He said the problem was fixed within minutes.

This is not the first attack of this kind. Last month, hackers took remote control of cooling systems at hundreds of stores in France. Remote control means controlling something from far away, through the internet. The French attacks seemed to target old systems. So far, no one has said who is behind the new attacks. The cases show that everyday machines connected to the internet can become targets. A cyberattack, or an attack on computer systems, can cause real damage in the physical world.
To sum up, apparent cyberattacks disrupted fridges and freezers at supermarkets in five European countries, and some stores had to throw out food.
Thank you for listening.

스웨덴에서는 ICA 그룹이 일부 매장이 피해를 입었다고 밝혔습니다. 또 다른 체인 쿱은 매장 6곳에서 문제가 생겼다고 알렸습니다. 벨기에에서는 체인 델하이즈가 이를 'IT 사고'라고 불렀습니다. 이 사고로 대부분 벨기에, 일부는 룩셈부르크에 있는 수십 개 매장이 피해를 입었습니다. 까르푸 벨기에는 700여 개 매장 가운데 15곳이 공격받았다고 밝혔습니다. 에스토니아에서는 냉각 기술을 만드는 회사의 대표가 공격자들이 냉장고를 제어하는 컴퓨터에 침입했다고 말했습니다. 그는 문제가 몇 분 안에 해결됐다고 말했습니다.

이런 공격은 처음이 아닙니다. 지난달 해커들은 프랑스의 매장 수백 곳에서 냉각 시스템을 원격 조종했습니다. 원격 조종이란 인터넷을 통해 멀리서 무언가를 조종하는 것을 말합니다. 프랑스 공격은 오래된 시스템을 노린 것으로 보였습니다. 지금까지 이번 공격의 배후가 누구인지는 아무도 밝히지 않았습니다. 이번 사건들은 인터넷에 연결된 일상 기계도 공격 대상이 될 수 있다는 것을 보여 줍니다. 사이버 공격, 즉 컴퓨터 시스템에 대한 공격은 현실 세계에 실제 피해를 줄 수 있습니다.
정리하면, 사이버 공격으로 보이는 일로 유럽 다섯 나라 슈퍼마켓의 냉장고와 냉동고가 고장 났고, 일부 매장은 음식을 버려야 했습니다.

4.headline: Apparent cyberattacks disrupt supermarket refrigeration across Europe
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Supermarkets in five European countries have reported disruptions to their refrigeration systems in what appear to be cyberattacks, according to The Associated Press. Stores in Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia were affected, and some were forced to discard spoiled food after fridge and freezer temperatures were pushed far above safe levels. The disruptions were reported on Monday.

In Sweden, the ICA retail group said a limited number of its stores were hit overnight, though it declined to give a figure, while one ICA store in the town of Sjöbo said its units had been set to 50 degrees Celsius. Rival chain Coop reported problems at six stores. Delhaize described an IT incident affecting several dozen stores, mostly in Belgium and a few in Luxembourg. Its fresh and frozen ranges were temporarily limited, but distribution centers and deliveries were not affected. Carrefour Belgium said 15 of its more than 700 stores were affected.

In Estonia, the chief executive of Kitman Coldtech, which makes the affected technology, said attackers had gained access to a computer controlling a client's refrigeration and raised the temperature, but that the problem was resolved within minutes without significant damage. He declined to name the store. One outlet of the Selver chain was also affected, according to the report.

The incidents follow a wave of attacks last month in France, where hackers remotely took control of refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets and independent shops, apparently targeting older equipment. No one has publicly identified who is responsible for the latest attacks. The episode highlights how everyday equipment linked to the internet can become a target, with real costs for retailers.
To sum up, apparent cyberattacks disrupted fridges and freezers at supermarkets across five European countries, forcing some stores to throw away food, just weeks after similar attacks hit France.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.

스웨덴에서는 ICA 유통 그룹이 밤사이 일부 매장이 공격받았다고 밝혔지만 정확한 수는 밝히지 않았고, 셰보에 있는 한 ICA 매장은 냉장 설비가 섭씨 50도로 설정됐었다고 말했습니다. 경쟁 체인 쿱은 매장 6곳에서 문제가 있었다고 알렸습니다. 델하이즈는 대부분 벨기에, 일부는 룩셈부르크에 있는 수십 개 매장에 영향을 준 IT 사고라고 설명했습니다. 신선·냉동 제품 판매가 일시적으로 제한됐지만 물류센터와 배송에는 영향이 없었습니다. 까르푸 벨기에는 700여 개 매장 가운데 15곳이 피해를 입었다고 밝혔습니다.

이번 사건들은 지난달 프랑스에서 잇따른 공격에 뒤이어 일어났습니다. 당시 해커들은 수백 곳의 슈퍼마켓과 독립 상점에서 냉장 시스템을 원격으로 장악했는데, 오래된 장비를 노린 것으로 보였습니다. 이번 공격의 책임자가 누구인지는 공개적으로 밝혀지지 않았습니다. 이번 일은 인터넷에 연결된 일상 장비가 어떻게 표적이 될 수 있는지, 그리고 유통업체에 실제 비용을 안길 수 있는지를 보여 줍니다.
정리하면, 사이버 공격으로 보이는 일로 유럽 다섯 나라 슈퍼마켓의 냉장고와 냉동고가 고장 나 일부 매장이 음식을 버려야 했으며, 이는 프랑스에서 비슷한 공격이 있은 지 불과 몇 주 만의 일입니다.

5.headline: Suspected hackers send supermarket freezers into meltdown across Europe
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

A spate of apparent cyberattacks has left supermarket fridges and freezers malfunctioning across five European countries, according to The Associated Press, with retailers in Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia reporting disruptions. In several cases, intruders appear to have cranked up temperatures to levels that rendered chilled and frozen goods unsellable, forcing stores to write off spoiled stock. The disruptions surfaced on Monday.

The fallout varied from chain to chain. Sweden's ICA group acknowledged that a limited number of its outlets had been hit overnight, though it declined to put a figure on it, while one ICA store in Sjöbo said its units had been set to a scorching 50 degrees Celsius. Competitor Coop reported problems at six stores. Delhaize, meanwhile, characterized the episode as an IT incident affecting several dozen locations, chiefly in Belgium with a handful in Luxembourg; its fresh and frozen ranges were temporarily curtailed, although distribution centers and deliveries were spared. Carrefour Belgium played down the impact, saying just 15 of its more than 700 stores were affected.

In Estonia, Jann Mutso, chief executive of Kitman Coldtech, which manufactures the targeted technology, said attackers had broken into a computer controlling one client's refrigeration and pushed the temperature up, but the breach was contained within minutes and caused no significant damage. He declined to name the client, although one outlet of the Selver chain was reported to have been affected.

The latest disruption comes hard on the heels of a similar campaign in France last month, when hackers seized remote control of cooling systems at hundreds of supermarkets and independent shops, seemingly exploiting outdated equipment. No one has publicly claimed responsibility for the new attacks, and no culprit has been named. Even so, the incidents underscore an uncomfortable reality: as mundane equipment is increasingly hooked up to networks, digital intrusions can translate into tangible losses on supermarket shelves.

To sum up, suspected cyberattacks have disrupted refrigeration at supermarkets in five European countries, leaving some retailers to dump spoiled food, only weeks after a comparable wave struck France.

들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

3.headline: Busan cafe run by BTS Jimin's father to close in a year
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

A cafe in Busan that is very popular with K-pop fans will close in one year. According to The Korea Herald, the cafe is run by the father of Jimin, a member of the boy band BTS. The cafe announced the news in an Instagram post on November 1. The post said there were "365 days" left to spend with customers. The cafe did not give a reason for closing.

The cafe has become a special place for BTS fans. Busan is the hometown of Jimin and another member, Jungkook. So many fans visit the city to see places linked to the band. Inside the cafe, there are BTS goods, artwork of Jimin and gifts from fans. Visitors can write messages in guest books and buy merchandise. Merchandise means goods with a band's name or pictures on them. Sometimes Jimin's father even greets fans and signs autographs.

Why does this matter? Places like this cafe draw visitors from around the world. For many fans, the cafe is a way to feel closer to the singer and his family. In its post, the cafe thanked fans for their support over the years. It also thanked people who traveled a long way to visit. The cafe said it hopes the last year will be a precious time to make more happy memories together.
To sum up, the Busan cafe run by BTS member Jimin's father will close in one year. Until then, it hopes to share more happy memories with fans.
Thank you for listening.

4.headline: Fan favorite cafe run by Jimin's father to close after one more year
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

A Busan cafe that has become a pilgrimage site for BTS fans is set to close its doors in a year's time. According to The Korea Herald, the cafe, which is run by the father of BTS member Jimin, announced the decision in an Instagram post on November 1, saying it had "365 days" left with its customers. No reason was given for the closure.

BTS, a seven-member group, is one of the best-known music acts in the world, and the cafe has long been a must-visit stop for fans traveling to Busan, the hometown of both Jimin and fellow member Jungkook. Part fan space and part tribute from a father to his son, it is filled with BTS memorabilia, artwork of Jimin and gifts sent by fans. Visitors can leave notes in guest books and purchase merchandise, and on occasion, Jimin's father himself greets fans and signs autographs.

In its announcement, the cafe thanked customers and fans for their support over the years, singling out those who had traveled long distances to visit. It expressed hope that the final twelve months would be a valuable time for creating more happy memories together. The post gave no details about what will happen to the space afterward.

Busan, Korea's second-largest city, already attracts many tourists with its beaches and seafood markets, and for K-pop fans, sites linked to their favorite artists are often a key part of the trip. For many of them, this cafe offered a rare personal connection to one of the group's members and his family.
To sum up, the Busan cafe run by BTS member Jimin's father plans to close in a year, giving fans one last stretch of time to visit a well-loved spot.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Jimin's father to shutter beloved Busan fan cafe after one final year
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

A Busan cafe that has become something of a shrine for BTS devotees will shut its doors a year from now. According to The Korea Herald, the venue, run by the father of BTS member Jimin, broke the news in an Instagram post on November 1, telling patrons that it had "365 days" left in their company. The cafe offered no explanation for the decision, leaving fans to savor the time that remains.

Over the years, the cafe has evolved into an essential port of call for admirers of the seven-member group, one of the most recognizable acts on the global music scene. Busan, the coastal city where both Jimin and bandmate Jungkook grew up, already draws a steady stream of fans retracing the stars' roots, and the cafe stands out among those destinations. Equal parts fan hangout and a father's homage to his son, its interior brims with BTS memorabilia, portraits of Jimin and keepsakes sent in by fans. Visitors pen messages in guest books and pick up merchandise, and every so often, Jimin's father makes an appearance himself, greeting well-wishers and obliging them with autographs.

In its farewell notice, the cafe expressed gratitude to customers and fans for their loyalty, reserving special thanks for those who had made long journeys to drop by. It voiced the hope that its final year would prove a cherished chapter, filled with fresh moments of joy and memories forged together. The notice left open what will become of the space once the doors close, and no details were offered about any future plans.

For a city that already pulls in visitors with its beaches and bustling seafood markets, the impending closure means the loss of a distinctive landmark on the K-pop map, one that offered fans a rare, personal link to an artist and his family.
To sum up, the Busan cafe run by BTS member Jimin's father will close in a year, giving fans one final stretch to pay a visit to a much-loved gathering place before it closes for good.
Thank you for listening.
